rows.speaker: النحويون
rows.claim: Grammarians call an emphatic sentence a qasam, even when it is declarative, as in God’s testimony that the hypocrites are liars.
rows.anchor: وهو عند النحويين جملة يؤكد بها الخبر حتى إنهم جعلوا قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source counts seven places where God swears by Himself; elsewhere He swears by created things, such as the fig, stars, and constellations.
rows.anchor: فهذه سبعة مواضع أقسم الله فيها بنفسه والباقي كله أقسم بمخلوقاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Oaths are especially apt when answering denial.
rows.anchor: وإنما يحسن في مقام الإنكار

rows.speaker: أبو القاسم القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayri says God swears to complete and reinforce the proof: judgment is established by testimony or oath, and He has supplied both forms of evidence.
rows.anchor: قال الاستاذ أبو القاسم القشيري إن الله ذكر القسم لكمال الحجة وتأكيدها

rows.speaker: بعض الأعراب
rows.claim: A Bedouin, hearing God swear that provision and the promise are true, exclaimed three times that the Majestic had been angered into swearing, then died.
rows.anchor: وعن بعض الأعراب أنه لما سمع قوله تعالى ﴿ وفي السماء رزقكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One answer says such oaths elide an annexed noun: God swears by the Lord of the fig, dawn, and the other created things.
rows.anchor: أحدها أنه حذف مضاف أي ورب الفجر ورب التين وكذلك الباقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second answer says the Qur’an follows familiar Arab practice, since Arabs revered and swore by these things.
rows.anchor: والثاني أن العرب كانت تعظم هذه الاشياء وتقسم بها فنزل القرآن على ما يعرفون

rows.speaker: ابن خالويه
rows.claim: Ibn Khalawayh favors the answer that oaths invoke what is revered; nothing is above God, so He swears sometimes by Himself and sometimes by created signs pointing to their Maker.
rows.anchor: واستحسنه ابن خالويه

words: ولولا أن تصيبهم مصيبة بما قدمت أيديهم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apodosis is omitted: absent their excuse that no messenger was sent, punishment would have overtaken them.
rows.anchor: جوابها محذوف أي لولا احتجاجهم بترك الإرسال إليهم لعاجلناهم بالعقوبة

words: ولولا أن تصيبهم مصيبة بما قدمت أيديهم
rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Maqatil instead supplies the omitted apodosis as: a calamity would have struck them.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل تقديره لأصابتهم مصيبة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says that without this circumstance there would have been no need to send messengers and repeat the proof.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج لولا ذلك لم يحتج إلى إرسال الرسول ومواترة الاحتجاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the account of Moses’ mother, the omitted answer is that she would have disclosed her grief over him.
rows.anchor: أي لأبدت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction repeats an unexpressed first تملكون, then uses أنتم as the subject while the expressed verb explains the omitted one.
rows.anchor: فأضمر تملك الأولى على شريطة التفسير

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says bringing أنتم forward as a separate pronoun marks exclusivity: people are singled out for continual miserliness.
rows.anchor: لأن الفعل الأول لما سقط لأجل المفسر برز الكلام في صورة المبتدأ والخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted answer is that they turned away, as the following statement explicitly confirms.
rows.anchor: أي أعرضوا بدليل قوله بعده

rows.speaker: الكرماني
rows.claim: Al-Kirmani says the account in this sura came later than the first, so it sufficed to repeat the greeting here; if the events differed, revelation would report two occasions.
rows.anchor: قال الكرماني لأن هذه السورة متأخرة عن الأولى فاكتفى بما في هذه

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the apodosis is omitted and supplied explicitly in Surat al-Takwir and al-Infitar as “each soul will know.”
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري 2 حذف الجواب وتقديره مصرح به في سورتي التكوير والانفطار

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: For the oath by the sky with constellations, al-Zamakhshari supplies an omitted answer that the people of the trench are cursed, signaled by their being killed.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري 2 حذف الجواب وتقديره مصرح به في سورتي التكوير والانفطار وهو قوله ﴿ علمت نفس ﴾ 3 وقال في ﴿ والسماء ذات البروج ﴾ 4 الجواب محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the Fire passage, the doors open when its people arrive; the version without waw makes arrival the condition for opening.
rows.anchor: وكقوله تعالى ﴿ حتى إذا جاؤوها وفتحت أبوابها ﴾ 5 أي حتى إذا جاءوها وقد فتحت أبوابها

rows.speaker: ابن خالويه
rows.claim: Ibn Khalawayh calls the waw in the Paradise passage the waw of eight, claiming Arabs conjoin the eighth item with waw.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن خالويه هذه الواو تسمى واو الثمانية لأن العرب لا تعطف الثمانية إلا بالواو

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali rejects the waw-of-eight account: Hell’s doors were closed, so arrival triggers opening; Paradise’s waw is circumstantial, meaning they arrive with its doors already open.
rows.anchor: فقال أبو علي لا أقول كما قال إنما تركت الواو في النار لأنها مغلقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Stopping and resuming is a major discipline: it guides recitation, interpretation, inference, and avoidance of problematic readings; al-Zajjaj, Ibn al-Anbari, Ibn Abbad, al-Dani, and al-Umani wrote on it.
rows.anchor: وهو فن جليل وبه يعرف كيف أداء القرآن ويترتب على ذلك فوائد كثيرة

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar reports that the Companions learned where a stop was proper just as they learned the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: وقد جاء عن ابن عمر أنهم كانوا يعملون ما ينبغى أن يوقف عنده

words: ولولا فضل الله عليكم ورحمته لاتبعتم الشيطان
rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas marks a pause after the clause about God’s favor and mercy, saying the statement ends there.
rows.anchor: وروى عن ابن عباس ﴿ ولولا فضل الله عليكم ورحمته لاتبعتم الشيطان ﴾ قال فانقطع الكلام

rows.speaker: النحاس
rows.claim: Al-Nahhas supports careful stopping with a Prophetic rebuke of a preacher who stopped after “whoever disobeys them”; he should have completed the sentence or stopped after “His Messenger.”
rows.anchor: واستأنس له ابن النحاس بقول صلى الله عليه وسلم للخطيب بئس الخطيب أنت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Zarkashi notes that the stopping argument just cited is disputed and does not pursue the disagreement here.
rows.anchor: وفيما ذكره نزاع ليس هذا موضعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith about the seven ahruf teaches proper completion: do not join a verse of punishment to one of mercy, or a verse of mercy to one of punishment; stop at the punishment clauses in the cited examples.
rows.anchor: وهذا تعليم للتمام فإنه ينبغى أن يوقف على الآية التى فيها ذكر العذاب والنار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wind’s “everything” means everything the people cherished, not absolutely every existing thing.
rows.anchor: وقوله ﴿ تدمر كل شيء بأمر ربها ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Queen of Sheba was given everything she wanted or needed, rather than literally everything.
rows.anchor: وقوله ﴿ وأوتيت من كل شيء ﴾ أي كل شيء أحبوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mirage-seeker finds nothing of what he had imagined and estimated.
rows.anchor: وقوله ﴿ حتى إذا جاءه لم يجده شيئا ﴾ أي مما ظنه وقدره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad and Moses are first among their communities or in their particular sense, not the first believers ever, since earlier prophets believed too.
rows.anchor: ولم يرد الكل لان الانبياء قبله ما كانوا مسلمين ولا مؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The condemnation concerns some poets, not every poet.
rows.anchor: وقال ﴿ والشعراء يتبعهم الغاوون ﴾ ولم يعن كل الشعراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here the plural “siblings” means two or more brothers.
rows.anchor: وقوله ﴿ فإن كان له إخوة ﴾ أي اخوان فصاعدا

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The exegetes say “the gate” means one gate among the city’s gates.
rows.anchor: وقوله ﴿ وادخلوا الباب سجدا ﴾ أي بابا من ابوابها قاله المفسرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that the Bedouins believed applies only to a group of them.
rows.anchor: وقوله ﴿ قالت الأعراب آمنا ﴾ وإنما قاله فريق منهم

words: وما منعنا أن نرسل بالآيات إلا أن كذب بها الأولون
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs meant are those whose rejection would bring punishment on the rejecters.
rows.anchor: واراد الآيات التي اذا كذب بها نزل العذاب على المكذب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels seek forgiveness for the believers on earth, not every person without distinction.
rows.anchor: وقوله ﴿ ويستغفرون لمن في الأرض ﴾ أي من المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source adduces the angels’ explicit prayer for believers as a related formulation.
rows.anchor: وقوله ﴿ ويستغفرون للذين آمنوا ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only some of Muhammad’s people rejected the truth; the community included eminent Muslims such as al-Siddiq and Ali.
rows.anchor: والمراد بعضهم فإن منهم افاضل المسلمين والصديق وعليا رضي الله عنهما

words: الذين قال لهم الناس إن الناس قد جمعوا لكم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Neither occurrence of “the people” is comprehensive: the first group itself belongs to people and could not have spoken to itself as the second group.
rows.anchor: فإن الناس الأولى لو كان المراد به الإستغراق لما انتظم قوله تعالى بعد ذلك إن الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pilgrimage months phrase denotes two full months and part of the third.
rows.anchor: والمراد شهران وبعض الثالث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic may use a plural noun for a dual referent: “your two hearts” is expressed as “hearts.”
rows.anchor: اطلق اسم القلوب على القلبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another usage omits an annexed noun and places its genitive in its stead: ask the village’s people, what the messengers promised, God’s religion, or love of the calf.
rows.anchor: ومنه حذف المضاف واقامة المضاف اليه مقامه كقوله ﴿ واسأل القرية ﴾ أي اهلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In al-Rahman’s paired structure, the balance sits between the paired sky and earth; the passage then commands justice and forbids injustice in weighing.
rows.anchor: ثم ذكر العدل والظلم في الميزان فأمر بالعدل ونهى عن الظلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rahman uses dual sunrises and sunsets because the sura repeatedly presents paired creations and contrasts.
rows.anchor: وإنما افردا في سورة المزمل لما تقدم من ذكر الليل والنهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Muzzammil uses singular sunrise and sunset after mentioning night and day; this context makes singular forms better than dual or plural ones.
rows.anchor: فكان ورودهما منفردين في هذا السياق أحسن من التثنية والجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ma‘arij’s plural highlights God’s vast lordship and power to replace the people: He moves the sun through a different sunrise and sunset each day.
rows.anchor: لأنه لما كان هذا القسم سعة مشارق ربوبيته وإحاطة قدرته والمقسم عليه إذهاب هؤلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The changing effects of sunrises and sunsets visibly transform plants and animals through seasons and temperatures, showing God can likewise transform a people.
rows.anchor: فكيف لا يقدر مع ما يشهدونه من ذلك على تبديل من هو خير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A proposed aspect of inimitability is foretelling future events unknown to Arabs; the source lists predictions that came true.
rows.anchor: الثالث ما فيه من الإخبار عن الغيوب المستقبلة ولم يكن ذلك من شأن العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source rejects this as the sole explanation: that would make passages without predictions non-miraculous, although every sura is itself a miracle.
rows.anchor: ورد هذا القول بأنه يستلزم أن الآيات التي لا خبر فيها بذلك لا إعجاز فيها

words: تلك من أنباء الغيب نوحيها إليك ما كنت تعلمها أنت ولا قومك من قبل هذا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another proposed aspect is revelation of earlier peoples’ stories as though witnessed, despite the Prophet and his people not knowing them beforehand.
rows.anchor: الرابع ما تضمن من إخباره عن قصص الأولين وسائر المتقدمين حكاية من شاهدها وحضرها

words: تلك من أنباء الغيب نوحيها إليك
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier-stories explanation, like the previous one, is a genuine aspect but cannot account for all inimitability.
rows.anchor: نعم هذا والذي قبله من أنواع الإعجاز إلا أنه منحصر فيه

words: إذ همت طائفتان منكم أن تفشلا
ويقولون في أنفسهم لولا يعذبنا الله
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further proposed aspect is disclosure of inner thoughts without visible words or actions, including hidden intentions and the Jews’ refusal to wish for death.
rows.anchor: الخامس إخباره عن الضمائر من غير أن يظهر ذلك منهم بقول أو فعل

words: إذ همت طائفتان منكم أن تفشلا
rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya calls the sixth account—Qur’an’s ordering, sound meanings, and continuous eloquence—the correct explanation, shared by the majority and expert scholars.
rows.anchor: السادس وصححه ابن ( 1 ) عطية وقال إنه الذي عليه الجمهور والحذاق وهو الصحيح في نفسه

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Its wording is inimitable because God comprehends all language and meaning and knows how each word must follow the last; human ignorance, forgetfulness, and distraction prevent comparable composition.
rows.anchor: فإذا ترتبت اللفظة من القرآن علم بإحاطته أي لفظة تصلح أن تلي الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This account also defeats the claim that Arabs could compose a match but were merely turned away from doing so.
rows.anchor: يبطل قول من قال إن العرب كان في قدرتها الإتيان ( 5 ) بمثله فلما جاءهم النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic places the singular before the plural: wealth comes before sons when both are singular; when wealth is expressed as plural heaps, it follows sons.
rows.anchor: سابق على الجمع كقوله تعالى ﴿ المال والبنون ﴾ وقوله ﴿ من مال وبنين ﴾

words: وَقَالَ رَجُلٌۭ مُّؤْمِنٌۭ مِنْ ءَالِ فِرْعَوْنَ يَكْتُمُ إِيمَٰنَهُۥٓ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description with a single adjective precedes the clausal description: “believing” comes before the clause “concealing his faith.”
rows.anchor: ومنه تقديم الوصف بالمفرد على الوصف بالجملة في قوله ﴿ وقال رجل مؤمن من آل فرعون يكتم إيمانه

words: كمن هو خالد في النار وسقوا ماء حميما
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading supplies an omitted first member of a comparison: is one abiding in the Garden and given its rivers like one abiding in Fire and given boiling water?
rows.anchor: أي أكمن هو خالد في الجنة يسقى من هذه الانهار كمن هو خالد في النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other comparisons state both sides explicitly, as in the examples of the dead person given life and the person with proof compared with one whose deeds are beautified.
rows.anchor: وجاء مصرحا بهما على الاصل في قوله تعالى ﴿ أو من كان ميتا فأحييناه وجعلنا له نورا يمشي به

rows.speaker: صاحب الأقصى القريب
rows.claim: The author’s opponent says a condemnatory question can concern the future, and reads these questions as rejecting what people may seek or deny in any time.
rows.anchor: وخالف في ذلك صاحب ( 6 ) الأقصى القريب وقال قد يكون عن مستقبل

words: أَتَقْتُلُونَ رَجُلًا أَن يَقُولَ رَبِّىَ ٱللَّهُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Zarkashi says this contradicts the rhetoricians’ consensus: the cited questions refer to past actions; no evidence supports future reference, and the grammar of أتقتلون does not determine the intended time.
rows.anchor: وهذا الذي قاله مخالف لاجماع البيانيين ولادليل فيما ذكره بل الاستفهام في الآيتين عن ماض

words: أتستبدلون الذي هو أدنى بالذي هو خير
أَتَقْتُلُونَ رَجُلًا أَن يَقُولَ رَبِّىَ ٱللَّهُ
rows.speaker: ابن جني
rows.claim: Ibn Jinni notes that grammatical inflection can differ from the meaning; the future-subjunctive أن in “that he says” does not make the condemnatory question’s event future in sense.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكر ابن جني في التنبيه ( 3 ) أن الإعراب قد يرد خلاف ما عليه المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For rhetorical questions used in negative forms, the interrogative may disappear entirely, remain alongside another sense, or allow either reading; context decides.
rows.anchor: بالكلية لاينبغي ان يطلق أحد الامرين بل منه ما تجرد كما في التسوية ومنه ما يبقى

rows.speaker: النحاة والبيانيون
rows.claim: Grammarians and rhetoricians differ over whether an affirmative question used for acknowledgment asserts a fact or seeks the addressee’s admission despite the speaker already knowing it.
rows.anchor: وفي كلام النحاة والبيانيين كل من القولين

rows.speaker: الغزالي
rows.claim: Al-Ghazali repeatedly condemns approaches other than the Salaf’s and, in his final theological work, urges scholars and laypeople to adhere to the Salaf and their followers.
rows.anchor: وأفصح الغزالي عنهم في غير موضع بتهجين ما سواها حتى ألجم آخرا

rows.speaker: علي وابن مسعود وابن عباس
rows.claim: Ta’wil is also transmitted from Ali, Ibn Masud, Ibn Abbas, and others.
rows.anchor: وممن نقل عنه التأويل علي وابن مسعود وابن عباس وغيرهم

rows.speaker: الغزالي
rows.claim: Al-Ghazali says Imam Ahmad interpreted three passages; some later scholars denied this attribution.
rows.anchor: وقال الغزالي في كتاب ( التفرقة بين الإسلام والزندقة ) ( 2 ) إن الإمام أحمد أول في ثلاثة مواضع

rows.speaker: القاضي أبو يعلى
rows.claim: Ibn al-Jawzi reports that Qadi Abu Ya‘la interpreted “your Lord comes” as “your Lord’s command comes,” supported by the parallel wording about His command.
rows.anchor: قلت وقد حكى ابن الجوزي عن القاضي أبي يعلى تأويل أحمد في قوله تعالى ﴿ أو يأتي ربك ﴾

rows.speaker: ابن برهان
rows.claim: Ibn Burhan and other Ash‘aris choose figurative interpretation; the dispute turns on whether revelation may contain wording whose meaning is unknowable.
rows.anchor: واختار ابن برهان ( 6 ) وغيره من الأشعرية التأويل قال ومنشأ الخلاف بين الفريقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Zarkashi says interpretation is needed when evidence rules out the literal sense, since bodily form is impossible for God; Arabic metaphor lets reason and revelation agree in fundamentals.
rows.anchor: وإنما حملهم على التأويل وجوب حمل الكلام على خلاف المفهوم من حقيقته لقيام الأدلة على استحالة المتشابه والجسمية

words: ليس كمثله شيء وهو السميع البصير
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reason cannot contradict authentic revelation, but not every passage can be reconciled through a clear interpretation; some readings would be strained or exceed human understanding, so the final appeal is that nothing resembles God.
rows.anchor: مستحيل ( 1 ) المرام والمرد إلى قوله ﴿ ليس كمثله شيء وهو السميع البصير ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Hands” in these expressions stand figuratively for the whole people who act or expose themselves to ruin.
rows.anchor: وقوله ﴿ فبما كسبت أيديكم ﴾ ﴿ ولا تلقوا بأيديكم ﴾ تجوز بذلك عن الجملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fingertip term بنان can stand for hands and feet, just as fingers in the ears may represent the whole fingers rather than literal insertion of every digit.
rows.anchor: وقوله ﴿ واضربوا منهم كل بنان ﴾ البنان الإصبع تجوز بها عن الأيدي والأرجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source groups “free a neck” for freeing a person, the nose for the face, and taking by the right hand as bodily-part expressions for the whole.
rows.anchor: وقوله ﴿ سنسمه على الخرطوم ﴾ عبر بالأنف عن الوجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sin is assigned to the heart because it is the site of sinful belief; writing is assigned to the hand as the instrument, though the whole person sins and writes.
rows.anchor: أضاف الإثم إلى القلب وان كانت الجملة كلها آثمة من حيث كان محلا لاعتقاد الإثم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation supplies an omitted whole-person noun, since the perceiver is the person rather than the sense organ; perception is attributed to the eyes because they are its means.
rows.anchor: وقيل المعنى على حذف المضاف لأن المدرك هو الجملة دون الحاسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In these expressions نفس means the person himself: God warns people of Himself, and Jesus says God knows what is within him.
rows.anchor: وكقوله تعالى ﴿ ويحذركم الله نفسه ﴾ أي اياه ﴿ تعلم ما في نفسي ﴾

rows.speaker: ابن فارس
rows.claim: Ibn Faris reports a group’s view that من is partitive here: believers must lower their gaze from what is forbidden to see.
rows.anchor: وحكى ابن فارس عن جماعة ان من هنا للتبعيض لانهم امروا بالغض عما يحرم النظر إليه

rows.speaker: ثعلب
rows.claim: Tha‘lab glosses “stand the night” as pray at night, since standing is only one part of the larger act of prayer.
rows.anchor: وقوله ﴿ قم الليل ﴾ أي صل في الليل لأن القيام بعض الصلاة

rows.speaker: ثعلب
rows.claim: Tha‘lab says some of the warning means the worldly punishment, one part of a threat that also includes punishment in the afterlife; it does not deny the latter.
rows.anchor: فقال ثعلب انه كان وعدهم بشيء من العذاب عذاب الدنيا وعذاب الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says Tha‘lab misread the cited poem: its “some souls” means the speaker himself, one soul among many, and the line means he never returns to a place he has left.
rows.anchor: الثاني انه اخطأ في فهم البيت وإنما مراد الشاعر ببعض النفوس نفسه هو

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari recounts, with a caveat about the report’s authenticity, Abu Ubayda’s exchange with al-Mazani over whether the alif in عَلْقَى marks femininity or is an added letter; Ru’bah’s verse and its singular form prompted the dispute.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري ان صحت الرواية عن أبي عبيدة فيدخل فيه قول المازني في مسألة العلقي

words: فإما نرينك بعض الذي نعدهم أو نتوفينك
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People may accept that an entire threat is not carried out, so they have still less reason to object to only part of it; the sura’s later promise to show only part before death supports Tha‘lab’s reading.
rows.anchor: ان الوعيد مما لايستنكر ترك جميعه فكيف بعضه ويدل قوله في آخر هذه السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A part may receive the whole’s quality: error describes the whole person, while falsehood is specifically the tongue’s quality, yet both qualify the forehead metonymically.
rows.anchor: الخطأ صفة الكل فوصف به الناصية وأما الكاذبة فصفة اللسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Conversely, a whole person can be described by a part’s state: being afraid is a condition of the heart.
rows.anchor: وقد يوصف الكل بصفة البعض كقوله ﴿ إنا منكم وجلون ﴾ والوجل صفة القلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person is said to be filled with dread although dread resides in the heart.
rows.anchor: وقوله ﴿ ولملئت منهم رعبا ﴾ والرعب انما يكون في القلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “authority” is a proof that would guide them; its indication is called speech because indication accompanies speech.
rows.anchor: أي أنزلنا برهانا يستدلون به وهو يدلهم سمي الدلالة كلاما لانها من لوازم الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording “in darkness” evokes blindness because darkness is a concomitant of blindness, where another verse uses “blind.”
rows.anchor: وقوله ﴿ صم وبكم في الظلمات ﴾ فإن الأصل عمي لقوله في موضع آخر

words: ما تذر من شيء أتت عليه إلا جعلته كالرميم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The storm destroys whatever is judged to be destroyed, as the account clarifies by saying only their dwellings remained visible.
rows.anchor: أي شيء يحكم عليه بالذهاب بدليل قوله ﴿ فأصبحوا لا يرى إلا مساكنهم ﴾

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود وأبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Readings attributed to Ibn Masud and Ubayy replace انظرونا with glosses such as wait for us, delay us, or watch for us, and مشوا with passed or hurried through it.
rows.anchor: وروى ذلك عن ابن مسعود وأبى بن كعب أنه كان يقرأ ﴿ للذين آمنوا انظرونا ﴾ أمهلونا

rows.speaker: أبو عمر
rows.claim: Abu Umar says the Uthmanic codex in people’s hands has only one of these forms, and the scholars follow that codex.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عمر إلا أن مصحف عثمان الذى بأيدى الناس اليوم هو فيها حرف واحد وعلى هذا أهل العلم

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik permits reading variants such as Umar’s فامضوا and يعلمون/تعلمون, invoking the seven ahruf; he says disagreement is harmless and people once used separate codices.
rows.anchor: قال مالك لا أرى باختلافهم بأسا وقد كان الناس ولهم مصاحف

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Ibn Masud corrected a reader’s طعام اليتيم to طعام الفاجر, and Malik says he considers that reading acceptable.
rows.anchor: قال أقرأ عبد الله بن مسعود رجلا ﴿ إن شجرة الزقوم طعام الأثيم ﴾ فجعل الرجل يقول طعام اليتيم

rows.speaker: أبو عمر
rows.claim: Abu Umar limits Malik’s permission to outside prayer: readings outside the Uthmanic codex are solitary reports, not certain, though they should not be categorically rejected.
rows.anchor: معناه عندى أن يقرأ به فى غير الصلاة وإنما لم تجز القراءة به فى الصلاة

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik says a person who leads prayer using Ibn Masud’s or another Companion’s reading that differs from the codex should not be followed; Meccan scholars agreed, with only a rare dissenter.
rows.anchor: وقال مالك رحمه الله فيمن قرأ فى صلاة بقراءة ابن مسعود وغيره من الصحابة مما يخالف المصحف لم يصل وراءه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sixth account limits the seven ahruf to particular verses: أف can take seven case and nunation forms, while some expressions may allow nine; most verses do not.
rows.anchor: السادس أن ذلك راجع إلى بعض الآيات مثل قوله ﴿ أف لكم ﴾ فهذا على سبعة أوجه بالنصب

rows.speaker: ابن عبد البر
rows.claim: Ibn Abd al-Barr says scholars agree the whole Qur’an cannot be read in seven ways throughout; only a few words admit that many readings.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عبد البر وأجمعوا على أن القرآن لا يجوز فى حروفه وكلماته وآياته كلها أن تقرأ على سبعة أحرف
